correctness.rationale: Independent geometric reconstruction: the nine edges are the row-union-column crosses of the 3×3 array of vertices. All chosen crosses lie in one connected component, and the isolated cells are exactly the product of the unused rows and columns. The nonempty intersection poset in reverse inclusion is therefore the product of two nonempty face posets of a triangle boundary, ordered by used row and column supports. This is the cell face poset of ∂Δ²×∂Δ² and realizes to T². The 9 supports of shape 1×1 give S³ and empty lower intervals, the 18 of shape 1×2 or 2×1 give S¹ and two-point lower intervals, and the 9 of shape 2×2 give S⁰ and lower intervals that are subdivided square boundaries. Proposition 19 gives the base T² and the joins S¹*S⁰ and S⁰*S¹, hence precisely 27 S² and 9 S³. Equivalently, for the wedge lemma the nonempty intersection diagram can be made constant on all proper inclusion maps by homotopy equivalences: for each sphere choose a point missing all its strictly smaller subcomplexes, contract their union in the punctured sphere, and extend the homotopy to the sphere. The top term is the order-complex base, not a contraction of an actual empty set. A separate reproduction built the nerve from rectangle supports, checked its (9,36,36,9) counts and validated all 18 uploaded collapse pairs as data; the resulting (9,27,18) complex has cycle links, closed connected manifold incidences and rational H₂ of rank one, consistent with the direct torus proof. The integral homology, fundamental group and cohomology ring follow from the homotopy splitting, not the reverse.
residual_risks: The result concerns the ordinary nonequivariant coloring complex, not a general class of hypergraphs or an equivariant wedge.
The prior example's printed cup-product degree is inconsistent with two H¹ inputs. The present ring calculation uses its own wedge equivalence, not that sentence.

evidence: Lemma 17 computes each intersection sphere dimension from hypergraph components. Proposition 19 expresses the full homotopy type as joins of those spheres with lower-interval order complexes in the intersection poset.
The source explicitly leaves the lower-interval order complexes dependent on the underlying hypergraph; the cited example does not evaluate its complete poset or base order complex.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general wedge theorem is genuine pre-existing homotopy-level machinery, not just homology, but stating it for these nine edges leaves unresolved the topology of the order complexes. A further classification of the complete supports and identification of their torus is needed to obtain the specific wedge.

evidence: The authors give same-row or same-column S¹ pair intersections, diagonal S⁰ intersections and examples of empty triple intersections when meeting all rows or columns.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is a genuinely resolved case of the wedge formula, not a new wedge theorem. The product-of-face-posets topology or a valid nerve collapse is a mathematical argument beyond substituting sphere dimensions or reading off known Betti numbers.

value.rationale: Example 23 is a motivated uniform-hypergraph counterexample, not an arbitrary small arrangement. Its full integral homotopy type distinguishes a torus obstruction with explicitly quantified sphere contributions from the many complexes sharing its published additive invariants. It provides an exact homotopy benchmark, including the fundamental group and the origin of the nonzero product. No value is assigned to recomputing the already published ranks by themselves.
residual_risks: The calculation is for one particular prior example and does not introduce a general homotopy classification theorem.
